title: US AI-chip export policy: AI Diffusion Rule, H20/H200 licensing, revenue-share conditions and chip-location legislation
why_it_matters: AI accelerators are the fastest-growing chip category, and US rules on who may buy them change every few months: a worldwide diffusion rule was issued and then dropped, and licences for China-bound chips came with unusual conditions. These decide how much of the AI-chip market Nvidia, AMD and others can serve.
questions: What did the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule require, and has BIS formally rescinded it or replaced it?
What licensing policy applies to H20-class and H200-class chips to China since 2025, including any revenue-share or security conditions?
What data-centre validated end-user (DC VEU) and country-level arrangements (e.g. UAE, Saudi Arabia) govern large AI-chip exports?
What legislation on chip location verification or domestic-first supply (Chip Security Act, GAIN AI Act) has been proposed or enacted?
What have Nvidia and AMD disclosed about the revenue and inventory impact of these rules?
subquestions: Dates of each licensing change and its legal instrument (rule, licence condition, press statement).
Which conditions are public and which were only reported?
primary_sources: Federal Register AI Diffusion interim final rule (Jan 2025) and any rescission notice
bis.gov press releases on AI chips (May 2025 guidance, Jan 2026 H200 policy)
Nvidia and AMD 10-K/10-Q and 8-K disclosures on export charges
congress.gov bill texts: Chip Security Act, GAIN AI Act (to verify status)
White House AI Action Plan (July 2025)
open_questions: Were the revenue-share arrangements ever formalised in a legal instrument? (to verify)

title: US Entity List, end-user controls, VEU revocations and export-control enforcement
why_it_matters: Beyond product rules, the US blocks named companies (Huawei, SMIC, YMTC, CXMT and hundreds more) and punishes violators. Listing decisions, the 2025 revocation of licence-free status for Samsung, SK hynix and Intel fabs in China, and large penalties shape how suppliers screen customers.
questions: Which Chinese semiconductor entities are on the Entity List, Military End-User List or NS-CMIC list, with dates and licence review policies?
What did the 2025 revocation of VEU status for Samsung, SK hynix and Intel Dalian (effective 31 Dec 2025) change, and what licences replaced it (e.g. annual approvals)?
What does the affiliates (50%) rule do and what happens at the end of its suspension in Nov 2026?
What enforcement actions (BIS settlements, DOJ prosecutions, smuggling cases) have involved chips, tools or EDA, and with what penalties?
What licence volume and approval statistics does BIS publish for semiconductor items to China?
subquestions: BIS enforcement case list for semiconductor items since 2019 with penalty amounts.
Is there public data on licence processing times (INT-0010)?
primary_sources: Federal Register 2025-16735 (VEU removals, 2 Sept 2025)
Supplement No. 4 to Part 744 (Entity List, eCFR)
BIS Office of Export Enforcement press releases and settlement orders
DOJ National Security Division press releases (chip smuggling cases)
BIS annual reports to Congress (licensing statistics; to verify availability)
Samsung/SK hynix disclosures on China fab licences
open_questions: INT-0010: licence decision times and approval rates

title: US inbound and outbound investment screening in semiconductors: CFIUS, the Outbound Investment Security Program and related legislation
why_it_matters: The US can block foreign purchases of US chip firms and now also restricts US investors from funding Chinese chip companies. This shapes who can buy, merge with or finance chip businesses.
questions: Which semiconductor transactions has CFIUS blocked, unwound or conditioned (e.g. Lattice 2017, Magnachip 2021), and what do CFIUS annual reports show about semiconductor filings?
What does the Outbound Investment Security Program (31 CFR Part 850) prohibit or require notification for in semiconductors, and what are the thresholds?
Has Congress codified or expanded outbound rules (COINS Act or similar in the FY2026 NDAA; to verify)?
What presidential orders under Section 721 concern chip firms?
subquestions: Count notices by sector in CFIUS annual reports.
Which technologies (EDA, advanced packaging, SME) are covered in the outbound rule?
primary_sources: home.treasury.gov CFIUS annual reports to Congress
eCFR 31 CFR Part 800 and Part 850
Presidential orders prohibiting transactions (Federal Register)
congress.gov NDAA FY2026 text (to verify outbound provisions)
secondary_sources: CRS reports on CFIUS and outbound investment

title: US fab siting rules: federal environmental permitting, water and state incentive programmes
why_it_matters: Building a fab in the US needs air, water and waste permits and large water supplies, and states compete with their own grants and tax breaks. These rules and deals affect timelines and costs of the CHIPS-era fab projects.
questions: What did the Building Chips in America Act (Oct 2024) exempt from NEPA review, and which projects still needed NEPA?
Which Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and RCRA permits does a fab typically need, and how long have they taken for recent projects (TSMC Arizona, Intel Ohio, Micron New York, Samsung Taylor)?
What state programmes (Texas CHIPS Act, New York Green CHIPS, Ohio, Arizona, Oregon CHIPS, Idaho) fund fabs, and with what amounts and conditions?
How are water rights and supply handled for fabs in water-stressed states (Arizona)?
subquestions: Project-by-project table of state incentive packages.
Any public data on permit timelines?
primary_sources: congress.gov S.2228 Building Chips in America Act text
EPA and state environmental agency permit records (e.g. Arizona DEQ, NY DEC; to verify)
Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund pages (to verify)
Empire State Development Green CHIPS pages (to verify)
Oregon Business Development Department CHIPS pages (to verify)

title: Customs classification, rules of origin and the WTO Information Technology Agreement for semiconductors
why_it_matters: Most chips cross borders tariff-free under a 1996 WTO agreement, and a chip's legal 'origin' is usually where the wafer was processed, not where it was packaged. These basics decide which tariffs and controls apply to a given chip.
questions: What does the WTO Information Technology Agreement (1996) and its 2015 expansion cover for semiconductors, equipment and multi-component ICs, and which economies are members?
How do HS headings 8541, 8542 and 8486 (and HS 2022 changes) classify chips, MCOs and SME?
How do the US, EU, China and Japan determine the origin of a chip (diffusion vs assembly), with key rulings?
How do free-trade zones, bonded warehouses and duty-drawback schemes (Malaysia FIZ, Taiwan science parks, China bonded zones) work for chip flows?
subquestions: Collect CBP rulings on semiconductor origin.
Does China use a different origin rule (China Semiconductor Industry Association guidance 2025 on wafer-fab origin; to verify)?
primary_sources: wto.org ITA and ITA expansion texts and schedules
WCO HS nomenclature 2022 explanatory notes for chapter 85 (to verify access)
CBP CROSS rulings database
EU Binding Tariff Information database
China Customs origin guidance (to verify)
secondary_sources: CRS or USITC reports on ITA

title: EU and member-state export control and investment screening for chips, incl. the Nexperia intervention
why_it_matters: European governments can now block chip exports, screen foreign takeovers and even take temporary control of chip companies, as the Netherlands did with Nexperia in 2025, prompting Chinese retaliation that disrupted car-chip supply.
questions: What does EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821 allow member states to control nationally (Art. 9 national lists), and which states (Netherlands, Spain, others) have used it for SME?
What does the 2026 Annex I update add for chips, tools and materials, and when does it apply?
What does the revised FDI screening regulation require for semiconductors, and when does it apply?
Which chip transactions were blocked or conditioned by member states (Germany AWV: Elmos/Sai 2022; Italy golden power; UK is separate) and on what grounds?
What happened in the Nexperia case: the Goods Availability Act order (30 Sept 2025), court measures, China's export ban on Nexperia China, and the suspension of the order?
subquestions: Timeline of the Nexperia case with official documents.
Which Commission recommendations on economic security (Jan 2024 white papers, outbound investment review) touch chips?

eur-lex Regulation (EU) 2019/452 and revised regulation (to verify reference)

title: China industrial policy and domestic substitution: State Council IC policies, Big Fund I-III, tax incentives and local funds
why_it_matters: China has spent heavily since 2014 to build a self-sufficient chip industry. The rules and funds behind this decide how fast Chinese fabs, tool makers and designers grow and how much they displace imports.
questions: What do the State Council IC policy documents (Guofa 2000 No. 18, 2011 No. 4, 2014 Guidelines, 2020 No. 8) provide, especially the tax holidays by node (e.g. 10-year CIT exemption for 28nm and below)?
How large are Big Fund I, II and III, who are the shareholders, and where have they invested (fabs, equipment, materials)?
What local-government funds and guidance funds support chips, and how large are they?
What localisation targets or domestic-tool purchase guidance exist, and are they official or only reported?
How do STAR Market listing rules channel capital to chip firms?

MOF/SAT/NDRC/MIIT joint tax circulars implementing Guofa 2020 No. 8 (to verify circular numbers).
Which Big Fund investments failed (Tsinghua Unigroup, HSMC Wuhan) and what happened?

title: China's market-access levers against foreign chips: cybersecurity review, procurement exclusion, customs and energy-efficiency rules
why_it_matters: Besides export controls, China can shut foreign chips out of its own market through security reviews (Micron 2023), rules on what government and state-owned buyers may purchase, customs checks and official guidance to avoid certain imported AI chips. These affect how much of the Chinese market foreign firms can serve.
questions: What did the CAC Cybersecurity Review Measures and the 2023 Micron decision require of critical-information-infrastructure operators?
What government-procurement and SOE rules (reported 2024 guidance excluding Intel/AMD processors; Xinchuang lists) restrict foreign chips, and which are published?
What official or reported guidance has discouraged purchases of Nvidia H20/H200 (2025-26), and what legal form did it take?
Have customs inspections or data-centre energy-efficiency standards been used to limit imported chips?
What is China's Data Security Law / security review exposure for foreign chip firms?
subquestions: Separate officially published measures from media reports; record reported-only measures as reported_claim.
primary_sources: cac.gov.cn announcements (Micron review, Nvidia summons 2025; to verify)
Cybersecurity Review Measures (2021) text
Central Government Procurement Center lists (to verify)
Micron and Nvidia 10-K disclosures on China restrictions

title: Competition law and merger control in semiconductors: SAMR, FTC/DOJ, European Commission, KFTC, JFTC, CMA
why_it_matters: Chip deals need approval in many countries, and China's SAMR has become a decisive gate: it let Intel's Tower deal lapse and has opened a probe into Nvidia. Antitrust cases also set how chip firms can license and bundle.
questions: Which semiconductor mergers were blocked, abandoned or conditioned by which authority since 2015 (Qualcomm-NXP, Nvidia-Arm, Intel-Tower, AMD-Xilinx, Broadcom-VMware, Synopsys-Ansys, etc.)?
What conditions did SAMR impose (supply continuity, no bundling, interoperability) and how long did reviews take?
What abuse-of-dominance cases were brought against chip firms (EC Qualcomm, KFTC Qualcomm/Broadcom, SAMR Nvidia 2024-25, Qualcomm-Autotalks 2025), with outcomes?
Is there evidence merger review is used as a geopolitical lever?
subquestions: Table: deal, authority, decision, date, conditions.

ftc.gov case pages (Nvidia/Arm)

title: Taiwan semiconductor regime: tax incentives, N-1 overseas technology rule, core key technologies, export controls and outbound investment review
why_it_matters: Taiwan makes most of the world's leading-edge chips. Its laws on tax credits, on keeping the newest process technology at home (the 'N-1' rule), on protecting core technologies and on approving TSMC's overseas fabs decide how fast leading-edge capacity can move abroad.
questions: What do Article 10-2 (tax credits) and the 2025 amendment including Article 22 (overseas investment/technology control, N-1) of the Statute for Industrial Innovation provide, and has Article 22 entered into force?
What are the national core key technologies under the National Security Act (NSTC list), and what penalties apply to leakage?
How does the MOEA Department of Investment Review approve outbound investments (TSMC Arizona, Japan, Germany) and what conditions has it set?
What do Taiwan's strategic high-tech commodities controls and entity list (Huawei, SMIC added June 2025) cover?
What rules restrict PRC investment and talent poaching in Taiwan's chip sector (Cross-Strait Act enforcement)?
How are water and power allocated to fabs during shortages (Water Resources Agency rules)?
subquestions: Legislative Yuan amendment texts and Executive Yuan effective-date orders.
Prosecution cases for core-technology leakage (e.g. 2025 TSMC 2nm case; to verify).
primary_sources: law.moj.gov.tw Statute for Industrial Innovation and National Security Act texts
MOEA Department of Investment Review approval announcements
MOEA International Trade Administration SHTC entity list

title: South Korea semiconductor regime: K-Chips Act credits, Semiconductor Special Act, national core technology protection and export controls
why_it_matters: Korea hosts the two largest memory makers. Its tax credits, cluster support, and strict rules on transferring 'national core technologies' abroad shape Samsung's and SK hynix's investment and overseas choices.
questions: What credit rates apply under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act for national strategic technologies (Feb 2025 amendment), and what is the estimated revenue cost?

title: India semiconductor regime: India Semiconductor Mission schemes, ISM 2.0, state policies, customs and SCOMET controls
why_it_matters: India is funding its first commercial fabs and many assembly-and-test plants with up to half of project cost from the centre plus state top-ups. The scheme rules and approvals decide which projects are viable and how fast they progress.
